Trademark usage

Non-GMO Project Verified trademark usage

How to use the Non-GMO Project Verified Mark and the other Non-GMO Project trademarks on packaging, websites and marketing. The Mark tells shoppers that a product has met the Non-GMO Project Standard. Using it correctly keeps that promise clear.

Who this is for: Participants with a signed license agreement and Non-GMO Project Verified products. Also covers retailers, wholesalers and industry partners.

Based on: Non-GMO Project Trademark Use Guide v2.2. Where this page and the guide differ, the guide wins.

Questions: Client Experience Team, verification@nongmoproject.org

Before you start

  • Only verified products carry the Mark. The Product Verification Program verifies individual products, not brands or companies. Every product shown or named next to the Mark must be Non-GMO Project Verified.
  • You need a signed license agreement. Using the trademarks on products or in marketing (ads, website listings, social media) is limited to licensees who have signed an agreement with the Non-GMO Project. Using them without one is trademark infringement and a breach of the license agreement.
  • Never use the Mark before verification. Showing it on packaging or marketing before a product is verified is strictly prohibited.
  • Ask when in doubt. Send questions about packaging or any other use to verification@nongmoproject.org for approval.

The trademarks

TrademarkWhat it is
Non-GMO Project Verified MarkThe seal on verified products. The one trademark participants use on pack
Non-GMO Project nameCan be written in plain text only. Never redraw or stylize it
Non-GMO Project logoThe organization's logo (butterfly and wordmark). Not for use with verified products
"Look for the Butterfly"A tagline that brands are encouraged to use in ads and promotions, set in Lora

Verification Mark versions

Also available from the Client Experience Team:

  • French Mark. For packages of verified products typically sold in Canada. Use it alone, next to the English Mark, or with a non-competing claim. You are responsible for meeting the applicable laws and regulations; see your license agreement.
  • Mark for FSIS. For verified single-ingredient products sold in the U.S. that need approval from the USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS). It must always appear with this text: "[Animal] Raised & Fed a Diet in Compliance with the Non-GMO Project Standard for Avoidance of Genetically Engineered Ingredients." Never use it on non-FSIS products or without the required text. Products sold only in Canada do not need FSIS artwork.

Artwork files are released after you complete enrollment and sign the license agreement. They come in full color and single color (black and white) as EPS, JPG, PNG and PDF. Other file types are available on request. If a creative agency is preparing your artwork, the Non-GMO Project needs your written authorization before it can send files to them.

Specifications

RuleDetail
Full color firstThe full-color Mark is the most recognized and is recommended
Single colorIf full-color printing is a problem, use the single-color Mark with its keyline, in black or white only
White is part of the MarkWhen printing the full-color Mark on a colored or clear substrate, print the white as a spot color. Never let the background show through the full-color Mark
URLThe URL at the bottom of the Mark is required and must stay readable
Clear spaceKeep a space equal to the height of the capital "N" in "Non-GMO" on every side, measured from the white edge. No text or graphic may touch the Mark or enter that space. The space scales with the Mark
Minimum size, English and French3/8 inch tall and 1/2 inch wide
Minimum size, bilingual3/8 inch tall and 3/4 inch wide
Minimum size, on screenLarge enough that the URL can be read.
Brand hierarchyThe Mark must never look like the name of your business or product. Keep it smaller than your own logo and lower in the layout

Incorrect uses

These are the most common mistakes. The list is not complete; if a use is not covered here, ask first.

  • Don't add gradients, drop shadows or glow effects.
  • Don't remove the URL.
  • Don't change the colors.
  • Don't place the full-color Mark on a transparent background. The white must be there.
  • Don't squish, stretch or rotate the Mark.
  • Don't use a low-resolution or low-quality file.
  • Don't remove the keyline from a single-color Mark.
  • Don't add a decorative border.
  • Don't recreate or stylize "Non-GMO Project" or "Non-GMO Project Verified". Write these claims in plain text only.
  • Don't crop the Mark or use only part of it.
  • Don't use a crossed-out "GMO" symbol. It implies a complete absence claim, which the Non-GMO Project Standard does not allow.

Type with the Mark

When you add text next to the Mark, use the Non-GMO Project typefaces:

  • Avenir (Book, Book Oblique, Black) is the Mark's primary font. Use it for promotional text next to the Mark.
  • Lora (Regular, Italic, Bold, Medium Italic) is for body copy and the tagline Look for the Butterfly.

Both are licensed for personal and commercial use through Adobe Fonts and Google Fonts. The Non-GMO Project cannot transfer fonts to you; you are responsible for your own font licenses.

Text next to the Mark

You may add text that reminds shoppers to look for the Mark. Acceptable examples:

  • "Look for the Butterfly"
  • "See our full list of Non-GMO Project Verified products at www.nongmoproject.org"
  • "X number of our products are now Non-GMO Project Verified"

Marketing and websites

Brand hierarchy keeps your materials compliant. The Mark is a product certification and a registered trademark, so:

  • It must always be less prominent than everything else in the piece.
  • It must never be mistaken for another company's or organization's identity.
  • It can be smaller than other logos and placed lower in the layout.
  • It must never suggest that the Non-GMO Project endorses anything other than the verified products.

Good ways to show verification online:

  • Show the Mark next to a list of all your verified products.
  • Show the Mark next to other certifications, with a note that each product is evaluated separately.
  • Create a page about your commitment to ingredient transparency and non-GMO products.

The Mark can also appear on ads, sell sheets, in-store signage, coupons, point-of-purchase materials, trade show displays and social media posts, as long as they are about verified products.

Not allowed on company stationery. The Mark refers to products, not companies, so it never goes on letterhead, fax covers, email signatures, business cards, folders, envelopes or memo cards.

Two exceptions:

  • Company reports: the Mark may appear on the pages that refer to Non-GMO Project Verified products, and only those pages.
  • Wholesale supplier email signatures: allowed if Non-GMO Project verification applies to your entire product line.

Accurate and truthful claims

Labels on verified products must be accurate, truthful and not misleading.

ClaimRule
In processNever promote "in process" status on packaging or marketing. You may talk about working toward verification in conversation, but never next to the Mark
GMO freeNot allowed, nor are similar claims such as "zero GMOs" or "100% no GMOs". They are not legally or scientifically defensible. The Non-GMO Project claim is a true statement that acknowledges contamination risk while assuring shoppers the product complies with the Standard
First and onlyNot allowed, for example "first Non-GMO Project Verified potato chip" or "only Non-GMO Project Verified pasta". With many technical administrators verifying thousands of products, these claims cannot be confirmed
Competing certificationsNo other non-GMO certification may appear with the Non-GMO Project trademarks. Plain text such as "non-GMO" that is not tied to another organization is fine
Bioengineered food disclosureNever use the trademarks on any product, display or material that also carries a bioengineered food disclosure under the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (NBFDS)

Questions

The Non-GMO Project monitors use of the Mark on packaging and in promotion, and acts to protect its integrity. If you are unsure about a use, or notice possible misuse, contact the Client Experience Team at verification@nongmoproject.org. They can help with packaging, messaging, marketing materials, campaigns and promotions.
